content: Welcome to this explainer on LSAT conditional logic. We will focus on rules, not blind word memorization. We will cover what a rule provides, direction, sufficient and necessary conditions and two indicator groups. Section one, what a rule gives you. We have to start by understanding logical guarantees. Let's take a basic rule. All dogs are mammals. This guarantees a very specific relationship. A rule tells you what must be true. A fact like Luna being a dog applies it. Now put it perfectly inside a cobalt box of mammals. When we put Luna inside that dog, she has to be a mammal, too. Section two, rules have a direction. Let's explore why these rules flow one specific way. An arrow shows a relationship. It absolutely does not mean cause or time order. The rule allows mammals that are not dogs. So, we cannot just reverse the direction. Section three, sufficient and necessary. The crucial point is understanding both sides of this logical relationship. Sufficient simply means enough. Being a dog is enough to guarantee it is a mammal. Necessary means required. A dog is required to be a mammal. This required condition goes right. Section four, group one indicators. Let's see how specific words introduce these conditions. These group on words introduce the sufficient condition that goes on the left side. Never blindly assign words after an indicator. Always ask what complete idea it actually targets. Here the word every refers to volunteers. So volunteers go on the left side. Section five group two indicators. Let's see how we find the necessary condition instead. Group two words introduce the necessary idea. That required idea always goes on the right. Ask what the require idea is do not just apply a mechanical word rule. Let's compare two similar sentences to see how the logic operates in real life. Both mean admission requires being a member. They share the exact same directional relationship. You have to read the whole statement before deciding where each complete idea belongs. Always ask if the rule gives you this exact result. Have you verified the complete meaning?
